name: Okatsune 101
recommendationLabel: Best overall for genuinely small hands (editorial)

handSize.notes: Okatsune hand guide: 16–18.5 cm length, 7–8.5 cm palm width (src-okatsune-uk-hand-guide)

weightG.notes: Okatsune Europe lists 177 g; Okatsune UK shop lists 180 g. Shown as approx. 177–180 g.

bestFor: Gardeners with genuinely small hands who want the most compact Okatsune model and highest published cut capacity in this group.
limitations: Right-hand-centric market positioning in some regions; verify feel if you are left-handed
Japanese steel blades require proper sharpening technique (manufacturer warns about bolt adjustment)
We did not hands-on test fit or cutting performance
whyWeLikeIt: Okatsune explicitly positions the 101 as the most compact of its three secateur sizes
Published 25 mm capacity exceeds FELCO 14/15 on paper
Manufacturer publishes hand measurement ranges for model 101
whoShouldBuy: Shoppers whose hand measurements fall near Okatsune's 101 guideline and who prioritize compact size and rated cutting capacity.
whoShouldSkip: Users who need Swiss-style service networks, rotating handles, or verified lightweight budget options.

name: FELCO 14

weightG.notes: FELCO lists 0.19 kg (190 g) net weight

keyFeatures: Lifetime warranty on forged aluminum handles (manufacturer terms apply)
Wire-cutting notch and sap groove (Gardeners' World)
bestFor: Small-handed gardeners who want a premium, serviceable bypass pruner with strong independent recognition.
limitations: 18 mm rated capacity—lower than Okatsune 101 or FELCO 6 on paper
Gardeners' World noted a stiff safety catch and struggle on thicker stems in their testing
whyWeLikeIt: FELCO officially classifies the 14 as Small at 180 mm
Gardeners' World independently reviewed it as light and comfortable for smaller hands
Strong serviceability story: replaceable parts and maintenance service
whoShouldBuy: Buyers investing in a long-term tool who fit FELCO Small and prioritize build quality over maximum rated cut diameter.
whoShouldSkip: Left-handed users, budget-first shoppers, or anyone regularly cutting stems near 20 mm+ without upgrading capacity.

name: Darlac DP930

handSize.value: Small hands / slim profile handles (manufacturer positioning)

weightG.notes: Primary copy and PDF list 146 g; Darlac product page WooCommerce field lists 178 g; some retailers list 145–170 g. VERIFY before citing a single number.

bestFor: Budget-conscious gardeners with small hands who want a lightweight bypass pruner for light pruning.
limitations: Lowest cutting capacity in this comparison (16 mm)
Weight data CONFLICT across manufacturer fields—verify on a current listing or scale
Less premium service ecosystem than FELCO
No independent lab test cited here
whyWeLikeIt: Shortest tool in the group at 175 mm per Darlac
Explicitly marketed for small hands with slim handles
Manufacturer PDF aligns with 146 g when the on-page conflict is ignored
whoShouldBuy: Light-duty pruners with small hands who prioritize handle slimness and lower cost over maximum capacity or premium service.
whoShouldSkip: Anyone regularly cutting thick stems, or shoppers who need a verified exact weight before purchase.

name: FELCO 15

weightG.notes: FELCO lists 252.5 g net; user research cited 252–254 g range

bestFor: Small-handed users who want FELCO build quality with a rotating handle to spread cutting force.
limitations: Heaviest Small FELCO in this list (~252.5 g)
Rotating-handle force reduction is a manufacturer claim—not independently verified here
whyWeLikeIt: FELCO positions the 15 for smaller hand sizes with ergonomic rotating handle
Useful when wrist fatigue matters more than minimum weight
whoShouldBuy: Ergonomic-focused pruners with small hands doing extended sessions who accept extra weight for the rotating grip.
whoShouldSkip: Shoppers wanting the lightest tool, left-handed users, or anyone satisfied with a fixed-handle FELCO 14.
editorialNotes: FELCO says the rotating handle can reduce the cutting force required by up to 30%—a manufacturer claim, not an independent test result on this page.

name: FELCO 6
recommendationLabel: Best for small-to-medium hands / higher capacity (editorial)

handSize.notes: Third-party articles sometimes mention suitability for smaller hands seeking capacity; we do not override FELCO Medium label.

keyFeatures: 20 mm cutting diameter—highest in this FELCO pair comparison
Lifetime warranty on forged aluminum handles (manufacturer terms apply)
bestFor: Users with small-to-medium hands who want more FELCO cutting capacity without jumping to large-hand models.
limitations: Not classified as Small by FELCO—195 mm may feel long for very small hands
whyWeLikeIt: Highest published cutting capacity among FELCO models here (20 mm)
Strong manufacturer spec sheet and widespread independent recommendations for general-purpose FELCO quality
whoShouldBuy: Gardeners whose hands are at the upper end of small or into medium range who prioritize capacity and FELCO serviceability.
whoShouldSkip: Very small hands that match Okatsune 101 guidelines or FELCO Small without needing extra reach.
